To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) We propose a novel algorithmic solution to the problem of perfectly-secure communication between two vertices in a network in the absence of any secure infrastructure; (2) We prove that our algorithm is competitive online and that a malicious adversary cannot learn anything more about the k-system than if it had learned everything about it after it had been built.
we propose and analyze a distributed and competitive algorithm for the problem of constructing edge-disjoint paths in a network, and prove that this algorithm is secure against a malicious adversary.

we propose a distributed and competitive algorithm for k-Edge Disjoingt Path Coloring, a generalization of a well studied problem, that is secure and bandwidth-efficient, and that the security of our algorithm holds even when it is attacked.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of algorithms for constructing secure communication structures in a network.
the following questions: 1) How can we use edge-disjoint paths to construct a secure communication infrastructure?
constructing a k-system that is resilient to a bounded number of attacks by a malicious adversary.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the algorithm we have proposed for the k-Edge disjoint path coloring problem is the first distributed, competitive online algorithm that is secure in a sense of not leaking information to an eavesdropping adversary, and that can be used for constructing k-systems for perfectly-secure communications.
we provide a provably secure solution for the problem of connecting pairs of vertices by a set of edge-disjoint paths.
our algorithm provides a bandwidth-efficient solution for perfectly-securing communication in the absence secure infrastructure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a bandwidth efficient algorithmic solution for secure communication, where the security is ensured by the construction of edge disjoint paths.

we give a bandwidth-efficient solution for perfectly- secure communication in the absence secure infrastructure, which is resilient to adversaries of bounded eavesdroppping capability, and is robust against malicious adversaries which attack the algorithm.
we provide an algorithm that can efficiently connect vertex pairs with a k-system and can withstand a malicious adversary.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the k-system is a powerful structure for constructing secure communication channels.
a network with low connectivity, but with high enough capacity, can support a high level of security.
a network can be made perfectly-secure with a bandwidth-efficient algorithm.
